# CLI reference

Every command, generated from the program itself. Run any command with `--help` to see the same text.

## `aiculator debug`

Debugging tools: verbosity levels, and changing them on a running server

```text
aiculator debug
```

## `aiculator debug levels`

Explain what each verbosity level shows

```text
aiculator debug levels
```

## `aiculator debug verbosity`

Show or change a running server's verbosity, with no restart

Changes take effect at once. Use --for, so that a debugging session cannot leave
the server logging at a high level by accident. The previous level then comes back by itself.

```text
aiculator debug verbosity [LEVEL] [flags]
```

**Examples**

```text
  aiculator debug verbosity                     show the current level
  aiculator debug verbosity 5 --for 10m         trace for ten minutes
  aiculator debug verbosity --vmodule engine=5 --for 5m
  aiculator debug verbosity 2                   set it for good
```

**Flags**

```text
      --for duration     go back to the previous level after this long
      --vmodule string   levels per component, such as engine=5
```

## `aiculator doctor`

Check this project's swarm for damage and leftovers, and fix them with --fix

Checks the data directory, even with the server down: a stale pid or address file, or a
server holding the lock without answering. With the server up, it also reports records repaired
at startup, records kept in quarantine, worktrees of finished tasks, and leases long past their
deadline.

Damaged task records are repaired when the server starts, with the originals kept. --fix removes
stale files and leftover worktrees. It never deletes a task or anything kept in quarantine.

```text
aiculator doctor [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --fix    fix what can be fixed safely
      --json   print as JSON
```

## `aiculator export`

Write tasks or other data to a file: JSON, YAML, CSV, TSV, Excel, HTML or Markdown

Exports what you choose, in the format you choose. Tasks are the default, and JSON is the
default format, unless the file name in -o says otherwise.

Values are always treated as text: HTML is escaped, Excel cells are stored as strings, and in
CSV a value that a spreadsheet would run as a formula starts with a quote.

```text
aiculator export [tasks|agents|usage|flow|realms] [flags]
```

**Examples**

```text
  aiculator export                                   # All tasks, as JSON
  aiculator export -o tasks.xlsx                     # The file name picks the format
  aiculator export --format html -o report.html --state running,review
  aiculator export --fields id,title,labels.team,owner --format csv
  aiculator export --label team=core --sort priority -o core.yaml
  aiculator export --with-meta --fields id,meta.points -o points.csv
  aiculator export --all -o everything.xlsx          # Tasks from every realm
  aiculator export --list-fields                     # What can be selected
  aiculator export realms --format md
```

**Flags**

```text
      --all                 tasks from every running realm, with a realm column
      --fields strings      what to include, such as id,title,labels.team; see --list-fields
      --format string       json, yaml, csv, tsv, xlsx, html or md; from the file name, or json
      --label stringArray   only with this label, as name=value
      --limit int           stop after this many rows
      --list-fields         list what can be selected, and write nothing
  -o, --output string       file to write; standard output if empty
      --sort string         sort by this field; -field for descending
      --state strings       only these states, such as running,review
      --where stringArray   only where a field has this value, as field=value
      --with-meta           add each task's properties, as meta.NAME; costs one request per task
```

## `aiculator import`

Load tasks once from a configured source, such as Jira, Notion or a spreadsheet

Reads a source named in .agents/sources.yaml, once, and creates a task for each item.
Importing again is safe: an item that was imported before is left alone, or brought up to date with --update.

```text
aiculator import SOURCE [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --config string   sources file; .agents/sources.yaml if empty
      --dry-run         show what would be imported, and change nothing
      --limit int       stop after this many items; 0 means all
      --query string    use this query instead of the configured one: JQL for Jira, a JSON filter for Notion
      --update          bring items that were imported before up to date
```

## `aiculator init`

Set up this machine, step by step: harnesses, skills and MCP config

Asks what you want, then does it. By default this sets up the whole machine: the swarm's
skills go where each harness reads them for every project, so that afterwards aiculator join
only has to start a server in a project. This needs no git repository and starts no server.

With --scoped it sets up this project alone, which also offers to start the server, and to
create the git repository the swarm needs.

Nothing is written until the last question is answered, so backing out with Ctrl-C changes
nothing. Running it again is safe, and keeps what is already there.

For a script, --yes takes every default, and flags answer single questions.

```text
aiculator init [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --all-harnesses    also offer harnesses that were not found on this machine
      --dry-run          say what would be done, and do nothing
      --harness string   set these up without asking: installed, all, or comma-separated ids
      --mcp              add MCP config without asking
      --no-mcp           do not add MCP config
      --no-skills        do not install the skills
      --no-start         do not start the server, with --scoped
      --planner          also allow these sessions to plan
      --sandbox string   sandbox for the server: auto, seatbelt, bwrap, docker or none (default "auto")
      --scoped           set up this project only, rather than the whole machine
      --tier int         tier for MCP sessions: 1 standard, 2 advanced, 3 ultra (default 1)
  -y, --yes              take every default and ask nothing
```

## `aiculator join`

Connect installed harnesses to the swarm: server, skills and MCP config

Sets a project up so any harness can join the swarm, including one already open.

It starts the server, and works on its own on a machine with nothing set up: it installs the
bundled skills into .agents/skills, links them to harnesses that need it, and registers the
MCP bridge. Anything a harness can already find is left alone, at either level, so after
aiculator init it only has to start the server. No secrets are written.

```text
aiculator join [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --harness string   installed, all, or comma-separated ids (default "installed")
      --no-start         do not start the server
      --planner          also allow these sessions to plan
      --sandbox string   sandbox for the server: auto, seatbelt, bwrap, docker or none (default "auto")
      --tier int         tier: 1 standard, 2 advanced, 3 ultra (default 1)
```

## `aiculator parallel`

Work out what subagents can do at the same time in one working tree

Worktrees keep tasks apart. This is the level below: one task split among subagents in one
checkout. Give it the jobs and what each will change, and it says what can safely run at once.
Jobs share a wave only if their claims cannot overlap, and a job that claims nothing runs alone.

This needs no server, and it does not touch the swarm's state.

```text
aiculator parallel
```

## `aiculator parallel plan`

Plan jobs into waves that cannot conflict

Reads jobs as YAML or JSON. A claim is a file or a directory ending in /. With symbol
granularity it can also be file#symbol or file:10-40. Reads are what a job relies on staying the same while it works.

Granularity is how finely claims are compared. The default, auto, uses the coarser of dir and
file that loses no parallelism, and it treats file#symbol as the whole file. To let two jobs share
one file, ask for symbol. Their claims are then checked against the file, but nothing can stop a
subagent straying, and two in one file can overwrite each other.

```text
aiculator parallel plan [flags]
```

**Examples**

```text
  aiculator parallel plan --file jobs.yaml -o plan.json
  cat jobs.yaml | aiculator parallel plan --file - --max 3

  # jobs.yaml
  jobs:
    - id: api
      touches: [internal/api/users.go]
    - id: docs
      touches: [docs/users.md]
      reads: [internal/api/users.go]
    - id: format
      exclusive: true
      deps: [api, docs]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --file string          the jobs, as YAML or JSON; - for standard input
      --granularity string   dir, file, symbol, repo or auto (default "auto")
      --json                 print the plan as JSON
      --max int              most subagents at once (default 4)
  -o, --output string        save the plan, for verify
```

## `aiculator parallel snapshot`

Record the working tree before a wave, without staging or committing anything

```text
aiculator parallel snapshot
```

## `aiculator parallel verify`

Check that a wave changed only what its jobs claimed; exits 1 if not

```text

```

**Flags**

```text
      --json           print as JSON
      --plan string    the plan saved by parallel plan -o
      --since string   what parallel snapshot printed before that wave
      --wave int       which wave just finished (default 1)
```

## `aiculator plugin`

List plugins, both compiled in and on PATH

Plugins compiled into this binary add commands, server routes and event handlers.
Build one in with a blank import in cmd/aiculator; the web dashboard is one, and go build
-tags noweb leaves it out.

Any program on PATH named aiculator-NAME also runs as aiculator NAME.

```text
aiculator plugin
```

## `aiculator realm`

See and name the projects on this machine that use the swarm

A realm is one project, with its own server and its own store. A project becomes one
when its server starts. Realms never share tasks or tokens, so trouble in one stays there.

Act on one from any folder with --realm NAME, such as: aiculator --realm shop task ls
See them all with: aiculator top --all, or aiculator web --all

```text
aiculator realm
```

## `aiculator serve`

Start the swarm server

```text
aiculator serve [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --addr string              listen address; port 0 picks a free one (default "127.0.0.1:7777")
      --aging strings            raise priority after a wait, as wait=boost, such as 1h=5,4h=20
      --aging-unit duration      waiting this long equals one priority point (default 1m0s)
      --branch string            branch that receives merged work (default "swarm/integration")
      --exit-grace duration      quiet time before agents are told to exit (default 30s)
      --lease-ttl duration       lease length (default 2m0s)
      --progress-ttl duration    time without file changes before an agent counts as a zombie (default 10m0s)
      --repo string              git repository to work on; empty disables the work layer
      --restart-grace duration   no lease expires this soon after a restart (default 15s)
      --sandbox string           sandbox: auto, seatbelt, bwrap, docker or none (default "auto")
      --standby                  if another server holds this data directory, wait and take over when it stops
      --sync-always              fsync every write; survives power loss but is slower
```

## `aiculator skill`

Manage skills in one place: .agents/skills

Skills live in .agents/skills. Installing puts them where each harness looks: harnesses
that scan .agents/skills need nothing, and the others get a link. Skills in .agent/skills
are picked up too. An edit in one place reaches every harness.

Patterns use * for anything, ? for one character and [abc] for a set. Quote any pattern
with a wildcard: an unquoted * alone also works, but zsh stops at an unmatched *-sth.

```text
aiculator skill [--install PATTERN...] [flags]
```

**Examples**

```text
  aiculator skill --install '*'                  all skills, to every installed harness
  aiculator skill --install 'swarm-*' 'lint-?'   by pattern
  aiculator skill --install '*-tool' --global    into ~/.agents/skills and home directories
  aiculator skill --install '*' --harness all    every supported harness, installed or not
  aiculator skill --install x --harness claude,pi
  aiculator skill --install x --path ./vendor/skills --harness none
  aiculator skill --install x --source ~/my-skills
  aiculator skill --list
  aiculator skill --lint
  aiculator skill --new my-skill --description "..."
  aiculator skill --uninstall 'swarm-*' --purge
```

**Flags**

```text
      --copy                 copy instead of linking, for tools that do not follow links
      --description string   description for --new
      --force                refresh bundled skills and replace links; your own directories are never replaced
      --global               use ~/.agents/skills and home directories
      --harness string       installed, all, none, or comma-separated ids (default "installed")
      --install strings      install skills matching these patterns
      --lint                 check skills against the Agent Skills spec
      --list                 list skills
      --new string           create a skill with full metadata
      --path strings         also install to this directory
      --purge                with --uninstall, also delete from .agents/skills
      --source strings       also read skills from this directory
      --uninstall strings    remove skills matching these patterns from harnesses
```

## `aiculator template`

Render reusable instruction templates into skills

Templates live in .agents/templates; .agent/templates and .agent/template also work.
They use Jinja2 and MDX-style components, and render into skills that install exactly as
aiculator skill --install does.

Bundled components: Directive, Anchor, Subagents, Backoff, OutputFormat, Flow, Step, Note, Toc.
Add or replace one by creating components/NAME.md in a template directory.

These produce instructions for a model. A model can still ignore text, so anything that
must hold needs a real check, such as a task's --check command.

```text
aiculator template [--install PATTERN...] [flags]
```

**Examples**

```text
  aiculator template --list
  aiculator template --new my-rules
  aiculator template --render agent-discipline --set retries=5
  aiculator template --install '*'
  aiculator template --install 'agent-*' --global --set timeout=300s
  aiculator template --install x --per-harness       a separate copy per harness
  aiculator template --install x --path ./vendor/skills --harness none
  aiculator template --check                         fail if a rendered skill is stale
```

**Flags**

```text
      --check             fail if a rendered skill no longer matches its template
      --copy              copy instead of linking
      --for string        with --render, render as this harness
      --force             replace links; your own directories are never replaced
      --global            use ~/.agents and home directories
      --harness string    installed, all, none, or comma-separated ids (default "installed")
      --install strings   render and install templates matching these patterns
      --list              list templates
      --new string        create a starter template
      --path strings      also install to this directory
      --per-harness       render a separate copy into each harness's own directory
      --render string     print one rendered template; writes nothing
      --set stringArray   template variable, as KEY=VALUE
      --source strings    also read templates from this directory
```

## `aiculator top`

Live terminal dashboard: flow, throughput, latency, jitter, probes, liveness and usage

A live view of the swarm. Keys: 1-5 or tab switch views, arrows or j and k scroll,
p pauses, q quits.

Without a terminal, such as in a pipe, it prints one frame and exits.
Rates reset when the server restarts. Task states and usage totals do not.

```text
aiculator top [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --all                 show every realm on this machine: 1 realms, 2 tasks, 3 agents
      --color               with --once: keep color even in a pipe
      --interval duration   how often to refresh (default 1s)
      --json                print the raw snapshot as JSON and exit
      --no-color            no color; NO_COLOR also works
      --once                print one frame and exit
      --view string         with --once: overview, tasks, agents, flow or usage (default "overview")
      --width int           with --once: width in columns
```

```text
      --harness string   installed, all, or comma-separated ids (default "all")
      --purge            also delete the swarm skills from .agents/skills
```

## `aiculator up`

Start the swarm server for this project in the background

Start the swarm server for this project in the background.

With --standby, also start a second server that waits and takes over if the first one
stops or dies. The leader is whoever holds the lock on .swarm, so the two never write at
once. Both must run on this machine.

```text
aiculator up [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --aging strings    raise priority after a wait, as wait=boost, such as 1h=5,4h=20
      --sandbox string   sandbox: auto, seatbelt, bwrap, docker or none (default "auto")
      --standby          also start a standby server that takes over if this one dies
```

## `aiculator web`

Open the web dashboard

Opens the live dashboard in your browser, using a read-only token that expires.

The dashboard is compiled into this binary; go build -tags noweb leaves it out.

```text
aiculator web [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --all            show every realm on this machine, for as long as this command runs
      --no-open        print the link and do not open a browser
      --ttl duration   how long the link works (default 12h0m0s)
```

## `aiculator work`

Work the queue from a shell: the route for any harness, no restart needed

```text
aiculator work
```

**Flags**

```text
      --agent string   agent name from aiculator work join
```

## `aiculator work claim`

Claim one specific ready task

```text
aiculator work claim [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --task string   task id
```

## `aiculator work fail`

Give up; saved work and note go to the next attempt

```text
aiculator work fail [flags]
```

**Flags**

```text
      --cost int      cost since your last report, in micro-dollars
      --lease uint    lease number from wait
      --note string   note saved for later attempts
      --task string   task id
      --tokens int    tokens used since your last report
```

## `aiculator work heartbeat`

**Flags**

```text
      --cost int      cost since your last report, in micro-dollars
      --lease uint    lease number from wait
      --note string   note saved for later attempts
      --task string   task id
      --tokens int    tokens used since your last report
```

